newsitem.title: USA: US Sen. Gramm says could overturn derivatives rule.
newsitem.headline: US Sen. Gramm says could overturn derivatives rule.

text.p: Senator Phil Gramm Tuesday expressed grave doubt about a new Securities and Exchange Commission rule on derivatives disclosure and said Congress could propose legislation to overturn the rule.
But the Texas Republican, speaking at a hearing here on Tuesday, said he had not decided whether to seek such legislation.

"There are many directions the committee could go in," Gramm said. "There are those who believe we have the ability to go back and overturn this regulation. And we certainly have the ability to make law."
"But let me say that I'm holding the hearing because I've not reached a conclusion on any of these items," Gramm said.

The new SEC rules would for the first time force public companies to disclose to investors use of derivatives, financial instruments whose value is based on the value of something else such as a commodity, stock or market index.
Gramm said he had many concerns about the new rules. The rules could discourage companies from properly using derivatives to reduce business risks, he said.
Gramm also said the SEC's cost-benefit analysis of the rule was lacking. "I am unimpressed," Gramm said. "It seems to me that this analysis was not well done and was not well thought out."
SEC Commissioner Steven Wallman was scheduled to testify before the Senate Banking committee's subcommittee hearing later on Tuesday.
